correction.text: not a Jabal Shammar shape before 1836

keyframe_review.note: 84,254 km2 (the Ha'il core) for 1825-1827, but the page says the emirate 'was established in 1836 as a vassal of the second Saudi state'; the Faisal page has Abdullah appointed Amir of Ha'il in 1835. Nothing on the pages opened describes a Rashidi state in 1825-1835. The same outline is used from 1836 (new keyframe).

correction.text: the Ha'il core, a nominal vassal of the Second Saudi State

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1836-1839: the Ha'il core of Cliopatria's 1840 outline (84,254 km2), the Rashidi vassal emirate under Faisal bin Turki. The page gives no area.
84,254 km2 for 1840-1841: the Ha'il province as a 'Nominal vassal of the Second Saudi State (1836-1848)'. The extent is not described on the page; the province is the minimal reading.

correction.text: the Ha'il core, not the Najd outline Cliopatria draws

keyframe_review.note: 459,743 km2 for 1842-1845: the outline coincides with the Emirate of Nejd's 1845 shape (1,793 of its 2,199 cells). The page has Ha'il a 'Nominal vassal' of the Saudis until 1848 and the Nejd pages have Faisal back in Riyadh in 1843; no page has the Rashidis holding Najd in these years. The Ha'il core is the shape to use.

New keyframe for 1846-1865, a gap in Cliopatria's Name: the Ha'il core, sovereign from 1848 ('Sovereign kingdom (1848-1921)') under Talal bin Abdullah (1848-1868). Faisal and the Rashidis stayed allied (Faisal page).

84,254 km2 for 1866-1876: the Ha'il core. Muhammad bin Abdullah (1869-1897) 'recaptured Al Jawf region which was seized by Faisal Al Shalaan during the 1860s' without a year, and the Ottomans 'installed an eighty-soldier troop' in the region in 1873 after its people asked for protection; neither is drawn. The shape is kept; the Jawf gain is recorded at confidence 1 in 1895.

135,542 km2 for 1877-1884: Ha'il plus 71% of Qassim. The page says the Rashidis and the Saudis 'engaged into a full scale war over the region of Qassim' and the Muhammad page has him ruling 'Qassim, Unaizah, Buraidah and Riyadh'; neither dates the Qassim takeover. Unverified: page budget.

222,015 km2 for 1885-1889: Ha'il, all Qassim and a fringe of Riyadh province. The Muhammad page: 'In 1887 he annexed Najd' and captured Riyadh, with a Rashidi governor; the Najd land stays in the Emirate of Nejd's shape, hatched Rashidi-held (that dossier's occupation event), so it is not added here.

375,103 km2 for 1890-1894. The Battle of Mulayda of 21 January 1891 ended the Second Saudi State and the Rashidis 'captured Riyadh and ruled Najd' (Jabal Shammar page). The shape holds for 1890 only; 1891-1894 is the new keyframe.

correction.text: the Jabal Shammar outline of 1890 and the Najd the Rashidis took at Mulayda

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1891-1894: the 1890 outline plus the Emirate of Nejd's last outline (114,136 km2), taken at Mulayda. The page's caption calls 1891 the emirate's 'greatest extent'.

union.text: al-Jawf, Tayma and Khaybar, reached by Muhammad's expansion

correction.text: the 1895 outline plus al-Jawf, Tayma and Khaybar

keyframe_review.note: 674,803 km2 for 1895-1904, Cliopatria's maximum: the 1891 outline plus about 730 cells of southern land (page silent). The page says Muhammad's 'expansion reached al-Jawf and Palmyra to the north and Tayma and Khaybar to the west', which the shape lacks (Cliopatria draws al-Jawf only from 1916), and that Ibn Saud took Riyadh back in 1902, so the Najd part ends in January 1902, not 1904. The correction adds al-Jawf, Tayma and Khaybar for 1895-1901 (Palmyra was a reach, not a province); 1902-1905 is the next keyframe. The infobox gives no area.

Riyadh and its oasis, lost on 13 January 1902

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1902-1905: the corrected 1895 outline without Riyadh, which Ibn Saud took on 13 January 1902 (the page says 1902 in one place and 1904 in another; the Emirate of Riyadh page says 13 January 1902). How much of the rest of Najd the Saudis held before Qassim fell in April 1906 is not on the pages; the shape keeps it until then.

union.text: al-Jawf, Tayma and Khaybar, reached by Muhammad's expansion

correction.text: the Ha'il core plus al-Jawf, Tayma and Khaybar, 1906-1915

keyframe_review.note: 84,254 km2 for 1905-1915: the Ha'il core only. The Unification page has the Saudis win Qassim on 13 April 1906 and the Najd remainder go to Ibn Saud by then, so the cut comes in 1905-1906, as drawn. That Rashidi al-Jawf, Tayma and Khaybar vanish in 1905 and return in 1916 is not supported by any page (none says they were lost); they are added back for 1906-1915.

259,971 km2 for 1916: Ha'il, al-Jawf, Tayma and the northern oases, as the page's account of Muhammad's reach and the First World War alliance with the Ottomans suggests; the 638 cells added to the 1905 outline are not dated by any page (ledger, confidence 1).
244,776 km2 for 1917-1919: the 1916 outline within 6%; the page names no change. Unverified: page budget.
244,175 km2 for 1920-1921; it ends with the surrender of Ha'il on 2 November 1921 ('Jabal Shammar was completely conquered by Saudi forces'). The outline passes to third-saudi-state.

ledger.note: 1836: Abdullah bin Rashid founds the Rashidi emirate at Ha'il as a Saudi vassal. Page: 'The Emirate of Jabal Shammar was established in 1836 as a vassal of the second Saudi state'; Abdullah bin Rashid had been appointed governor of Ha'il by Imam Faisal bin Turki (the Faisal page dates the appointment 1835). The vassal pair sits in emirate-of-nejd's ledger.

1877: most of Qassim passes to the Rashidis. Page: the Rashidis and Saudis 'engaged into a full scale war over the region of Qassim'; the Muhammad page has him ruling Qassim, Unaizah and Buraidah; neither gives a year, so 1877 is Cliopatria's.

region.text: Riyadh and Najd under a Rashidi governor

ledger.note: 1887: Muhammad bin Abdullah annexes Najd. Page: 'In 1887 he annexed Najd', attacked and captured Riyadh and appointed a Rashidi governor (Salim Al Sibhan) 'rather than restoring Abdullah bin Faisal'. The Mulayda page gives no date and has the Rashidis only 'planning' to conquer Qassim and Riyadh.
January 1891: the Rashidi occupation of Najd becomes annexation at Mulayda ('Following the battle he captured Riyadh and ruled Najd', Muhammad bin Abdullah page).

region.text: Najd and Riyadh, the last Saudi outline

ledger.note: 21 January 1891: the Rashidis win Mulayda and take Najd. Page: 'Decisive Rashidi victory', 'End of the Second Saudi State'; 'In 1891, after a rebellion, Abd al-Rahman bin Faysal bin Turki Al Saud left Riyadh' (Jabal Shammar page). The page's caption: the emirate 'at its greatest extent in 1891'.

region.text: al-Jawf, Tayma and Khaybar, reached by Muhammad's expansion

ledger.note: 1895 (any year 1869-1897): al-Jawf, Tayma and Khaybar are Rashidi. Page: Muhammad's 'expansion reached al-Jawf and Palmyra to the north and Tayma and Khaybar to the west'; he 'recaptured Al Jawf region which was seized by Faisal Al Shalaan during the 1860s' (Muhammad bin Abdullah page). No year is given, so 1895, where the corrected outline begins, is a bridge.

13 January 1902: Ibn Saud retakes Riyadh. Page: 'In 1902, Abdulaziz ibn Saud succeeded in recapturing Riyadh for the House of Saud' (the same page later says 1904; the Emirate of Riyadh page: 'on January 13, 1902').

minus.text: the 1895 outline plus al-Jawf, Tayma and Khaybar

region.text: the Najd remainder between Riyadh and Ha'il that Cliopatria's 1905 outline drops, page silent

ledger.note: 1905: the rest of Najd passes to Ibn Saud. The Unification page dates only Riyadh (1902) and Qassim (1906); how the Najd between them changed hands is not on the pages, and Cliopatria draws the cut in 1905 (bridge).
13 April 1906: Qassim falls to the Saudis. Page: 'decisive victory in Qasim on 13 April 1906', with fighting into 1907; Abdulaziz bin Mutaib was killed at Rawdat Muhanna in 1906 (Jabal Shammar page).

union.text: al-Jawf, Tayma and Khaybar, reached by Muhammad's expansion

region.text: the northern lands Cliopatria adds in 1916, page silent

ledger.note: 1916: Cliopatria extends the Rashidi outline north and west (about 640 cells in al-Jawf, Wadi Sirhan and the Tayma fringe). No page dates the extension; the Rashidis were Ottoman allies in the war (Jabal Shammar page). Bridge.

2 November 1921: Ha'il surrenders and Jabal Shammar is conquered. Page: 'The Emirate surrendered to the Saudis on November 2, 1921' (infobox 3 November) and was incorporated into the Sultanate of Nejd; Unification page: 'Jabal Shammar was completely conquered by Saudi forces'.

2 November 1921: the Rashidi emirate ends. Page: 'The Emirate surrendered to the Saudis on November 2, 1921' under Muhammad bin Talal, the last emir (1921), and 'was then incorporated into the Sultanate of Nejd'.

wars.name: Battle of Mulayda
wars.outcome: Decisive Rashidi victory on 21 January 1891: the Al Saud fled and the Second Saudi State ended.
wars.note: Muhammad bin Abdullah annexed Najd in 1887 on his own page; the Mulayda page gives no earlier date.

wars.name: Rashidi-Saudi war over Qassim
wars.outcome: The Rashidis held most of Qassim by 1877 on Cliopatria's drawing and lost it to Ibn Saud on 13 April 1906.
wars.note: The page dates no step before 1891; the Unification page dates 1906.

wars.name: Saudi-Rashidi war
wars.outcome: Saudi victory: Riyadh 13 January 1902, Qassim 13 April 1906, Ha'il 2 November 1921.
wars.note: Abdulaziz bin Mutaib died at Rawdat Muhanna in 1906; the Ottomans were Rashidi allies.

certainty.note: Tribal and desert frontiers throughout; the Ottoman alliance and the Saudi wars fix no line, and the pages name no treaty boundary. The northern reach (al-Jawf, Palmyra) is a sphere rather than a border.

sources.title: Emirate of Jabal Shammar

notes:
Cliopatria's Name starts in 1825 but the page dates the emirate to 1836 (vassal of the Second Saudi State) and to 1848 as a sovereign state; 1825-1827 is marked wrong, 1836-1839 and 1846-1865 are new keyframes (the Name has a gap 1846-1865), and the 1842-1845 shape is the Emirate of Nejd's outline and is marked wrong.

Disagreements on the pages: (1) the Rashidi takeover of Riyadh is 1887 on the Muhammad bin Abdullah page, 1891 on the Mulayda page, and the Jabal Shammar page prints 'The Rashid occupied the Saudi capital of Riyadh in 1865' in one place and 1891 in another; the ledger uses 1887 (annexation, hatched in the Nejd dossier) and 21 January 1891; (2) Ibn Saud's return to Riyadh is 1902 and 1904 on the Jabal Shammar page, 13 January 1902 on the Emirate of Riyadh page: 1902 is used; (3) the founding is 1835 on the Faisal page and 1836 on the Jabal Shammar page: 1836 is used.

Unsettled: when al-Jawf, Tayma and Khaybar became Rashidi (Muhammad's reign 1869-1897; the Al-Jawf Province page was silent), what the Ottoman troop of 1873 held, how the Rashidis lost the Najd remainder between 1902 and 1906, and who held al-Jawf between 1906 and 1916. The Palmyra reach is not drawn. No infobox area exists on the page. The page budget (5) was spent on Jabal Shammar, Muhammad bin Abdullah Al Rashid, Mulayda, Unification of Saudi Arabia and Al-Jawf Province (thin).

Region names the gazetteer lacks: Tayma (about 38.55 E, 27.63 N) and Khaybar (about 39.29 E, 25.70 N), used as 60 km discs; 'Jabal Shammar' is not a gazetteer region (the Ha'il admin-1 unit stands for the core).
